title.narrative: GAP phase 2, Min for HR and Refugees (FIGAP)

description.narrative: Stöd till Bosnien och Hercegovinas jämställdhetsmyndighet (Gender Equality Agency på statlig nivå och två myndigheter på entitetsnivå). Målet med insatsen är att genom standardiserad jämställdhetsintegrering uppnå att allmänna beslut förbättrar villkoren för kvinnor, män, flickor och pojkar i Bosnien på ett jämställt sett och att en standardiserad jämtälldhetsintegrering i BiH sker på ett öppet, ansvarstagande, jämställt och inkluderande sätt genom programmet (FIGAP2)

Support to the gender mechanisms of Bosnia och Herzegovina (Gender Equality Agency on state level and two gender centers on entity level). The objective of the contribution is to have a standardised gender mainstreaming in BiH in order to reach a situation where public decisions improve the conditions for women, men, girls and boys equally. The standardized gender mainstreaming should be done through a transparent, accountable, equitable and inclusive programme (FIGAP2).

The intervention aims at - "public decisions to improve the conditions of women, men, girls and boys equally". This should be done by standardisation of gender mainstreaming in Bosnia and Herzegovina (through transparent, accountable, equitable and participatory FIGAP2). There are four objectives of the programme, which all aims at improving gender equality aspects of public decisions in BiH: 1. An accountable GE policy framework in FIGAP priority areas (GBV, Economic Empowerment, public participation) 2. Capable GM structures for GE that perform according to their mandate 3. Effective systems that support the accepted GM approach 4. Competent and sustainable staff contingency in BiH to promote and manage GM agenda

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
According to the Gender Institutional Mechanisms (GIMs), FIGAP has enabled them to implement their mandates, something that could not have been fulfilled without the funds from donors. FIGAP II has implied more quality, deep and detailed work of GIMs and ensured that gender equality and gender mainstreaming have become an important issue.
Within their mandates, GIMs have worked to ensure gender mainstreaming in the public administration at different levels. FIGAP II has contributed to capacity building in relation to gender mainstreaming within institutions, so that they have been able to continue to mainstream gender on their own. FIGAP II partners report that thanks to FIGAP II, institutions pay more attention to gender equality issues and gender mainstreaming in their documents.
GIMs have review/gender mainstreamed/given an opinion on 370 legal, by-laws, strategic and other regulations. As GIMs always includes a reminder at the end of the document to fulfil requirements in the Gender Equality Law (GEL), the awareness and adherence to gender equality and gender mainstreaming has increased over time through such activity. Various strategies and action plans related to gender equality have been prepared by the GIMs thanks to FIGAP, and adopted, including the new BiH Gender Action Plan 2023-2027. Work on gender statistics have led to the development of the Gender Equality Index, that more institutions now collect and record data classified by gender, and that gender-disaggregated statistical data has increased...
The degree of participation of GIMs in consultations and working groups for drafting laws and sectoral policies has increased. Hence, during FIGAP II, the influence of GIMs (gender mainstreaming) has increased. GIMs close cooperation with line ministries and other institutions has led to more requests for support from GIMs from institutions, not only when drafting the documentation but also during implementation. More institutions have included obligations from the BiH Gender Action Plan into their regular work programs, such as educational and promotional activities for raising awareness on gender equality.
FIGAP II has contributed to coordination and collaboration within and between institutions on issues related gender equality. GIMs have continued to coordinate with and provided support to gender mechanisms elsewhere in the institutions, such as parliamentary bodies for gender equality and other committees.
Trainings on gender equality law for various institutions has resulted in greater willingness of the institutions and legislative bodies to plan, implement and monitor gender equality measures. The number of measures related to gender equality and gender mainstreaming adopted by the institutional partners increased. GIMs participation, support in and work in coordination bodies for different action plans resulted in strengthening of institutional capacities for the independent introduction of gender equality into the work. The number of institutions that keep gender-disaggregated data has increased. Civil servants in different institutions has gained knowledge and increased capacities on different topics related to gender equality. Modules on gender equality are now included in training programs for civil servants.
31 projects that contributes to the Gender Action Plan of BiH through grants to civil society organisations have been completed. The projects have been carried out in different fields and in different places in BiH. Projects have also contributed to mutual trust, partnership and joint action of NGOs and GIMs.
As a result of FIGAP II and GIMs activities, gender equality has increasingly becoming a priority and one of the cross cutting elements in all sectoral areas as well as in the EU integration process. New modules have been introduced for the training and education on gender equality related issues of civil servants, police officers and judges and prosecutors. Cooperation with the academic community has led to improved university classes on gender equality.
FIGAP II has implied a better coordination of work between the three GIMs, something that has been increaslingly difficult due to political reasons. This has also benefitted other projects outside FIGAP II, where GIMs participate or have an implementing role, as well as the "ordinary" work that is done by GIMs.
FIGAP II has been an enabler for other projects to be operational and also thereby contributed to results in these. GIMs have participated in programs and projects funded and managed by other organisations and donors, such as UN's Women in Elections project, the EU-funded Gender Equality Facility (GEF) project, USAID's project about gender-based violence, and projects and work by UN Women. Results from these projects have also been reported by the FIGAP II program, such as the development of the gender equality index and increased use of gender responsive budgeting in the public sector.
According to the GIMs themselves, FIGAP II has provided an important and unique opportunity for the GIMs to own their program, ie not cooperating with another organisation (such as the UN) who plans and controls the budget. The fact that FIGAP II funds go directly to the institutions and that the GIMs own the program beyond being a mere implementer has helped legitimize the GIMs vis a vis other institutions and prevented them for being politically outmaneuvered. With FIGAP II the institutions has managed to get attention to gender equality, which is generally not a prioritised issue..
